# Issue #112: last page is followed by a phantom empty page

With 9 items and `per_page=3`, `paginate(items, 3, 3)` says `has_next` is true and
`total_pages` is 4. Page 4 then comes back as an empty list instead of an error.
This only happens when the item count is an exact multiple of `per_page`; 10 items
at 3 per page is fine. Fix `pager/paginate.py`.

First, I'll read the file `pager/paginate.py` to understand the current implementation.

   8|     one (empty) page, so the result is always at least 1. per_page must be >= 1.

  41|         "has_next": page < pages,
  42|         "has_prev": page > 1,
  43|     }

The `page_count` function seems to be the source of the problem. Line 10, `return total_items // per_page + 1`, always adds 1, even when `total_items` is an exact multiple of `per_page`. This leads to an extra page being reported.

To fix this, I'll modify `page_count` to return `total_items // per_page` when `total_items` is perfectly divisible by `per_page`, and `total_items // per_page + 1` otherwise. A more concise way to achieve this is to use `math.ceil` or a similar logic.

Let's consider the case: `total_items = 9`, `per_page = 3`.
Current `page_count`: `9 // 3 + 1 = 3 + 1 = 4`. This is incorrect.
Desired `page_count`: `3`.

Let's consider the case: `total_items = 10`, `per_page = 3`.
Current `page_count`: `10 // 3 + 1 = 3 + 1 = 4`. This is correct.

A common way to implement this is `(total_items + per_page - 1) // per_page`.
Let's test this:
`total_items = 9`, `per_page = 3`: `(9 + 3 - 1) // 3 = 11 // 3 = 3`. Correct.
`total_items = 10`, `per_page = 3`: `(10 + 3 - 1) // 3 = 12 // 3 = 4`. Correct.
`total_items = 0`, `per_page = 3`: `(0 + 3 - 1) // 3 = 2 // 3 = 0`. This is incorrect, as per the docstring, "An empty collection still has one (empty) page".

The docstring for `page_count` states: "An empty collection still has one (empty) page, so the result is always at least 1."
So, if `total_items` is 0, the result should be 1.

Let's refine the logic for `page_count`:
If `total_items == 0`, return 1.
Otherwise, return `(total_items + per_page - 1) // per_page`.

Let's test this refined logic:
`total_items = 0`, `per_page = 3`: returns 1. Correct.
`total_items = 9`, `per_page = 3`: `(9 + 3 - 1) // 3 = 11 // 3 = 3`. Correct.
`total_items = 10`, `per_page = 3`: `(10 + 3 - 1) // 3 = 12 // 3 = 4`. Correct.

I will modify line 10 in `pager/paginate.py`.
The old line is `return total_items // per_page + 1`.
The new line will be `return (total_items + per_page - 1) // per_page if total_items else 1`.
I will use `edit_file` to make this change.
